plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a single right triangle drawn in plain black outline with no axes, grid, or shading. The triangle sits on a horizontal base labeled a beneath its midpoint. From the right end of that base a vertical side rises, labeled p on its outer edge. The hypotenuse slants down from the top of the vertical side to the left vertex, labeled h above its middle. A small open square at the lower right vertex marks the right angle between the base and the vertical side, and a single arc at the left vertex marks the acute angle, labeled with the Greek letter theta. The labeling is organized around theta rather than around the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite it, and h is the hypotenuse, so each name states a role rather than a direction. Carrying no numbers at all, the drawing serves as the reference diagram for recovering an unknown acute angle from two known side lengths, the given pair determining which inverse trigonometric relation applies.

interactionPlan.concept: The sides of a right triangle are named by their role relative to a chosen acute angle theta (adjacent, opposite, hypotenuse), and a known ratio of two side lengths determines theta through the matching inverse trigonometric function.
elements: right triangle in plain black outline, no axes or grid
horizontal base side labeled 'a' beneath its midpoint (adjacent to theta)
vertical side at the right end of the base, labeled 'p' on its outer edge (opposite theta)
hypotenuse slanting from the top of the vertical side down to the left vertex, labeled 'h' above its middle
small open square marking the right angle at the lower-right vertex
arc at the left vertex marking the acute angle, labeled 'θ'
role annotation labels (adjacent / opposite / hypotenuse) shown when a side is selected
inverse-trig relation label (e.g. θ = arctan(p/a) or θ = arcsin(p/h)) shown when a ratio is entered

interactions.teaches: Each side name is a role relative to theta, not a direction on the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite it, and h is the hypotenuse regardless of orientation

interactions.label: Angle θ (degrees)
interactions.teaches: Changing theta reshapes the triangle and shifts the balance between opposite and adjacent side lengths, while the labels a, p, h keep their roles throughout

interactions.label: Known side ratio (as a decimal, e.g. p/a)
interactions.teaches: A known pair of side lengths fixes theta through exactly one inverse relation — r = p/a gives θ = arctan(r), r = p/h gives θ = arcsin(r) (valid only for r ≤ 1), and r = a/h gives θ = arccos(r) — so the given sides determine which inverse trig function applies

demo_steps.title: Meet the roles
demo_steps.narration: Click each side in turn: a highlights as the side adjacent to θ, p as the side opposite θ, and h as the hypotenuse. The names describe positions relative to the angle, not to the page.

demo_steps.title: Reshape with theta
demo_steps.narration: Drag the θ slider. As the angle grows, the opposite side p stretches while the adjacent side a shrinks relative to it — the roles stay fixed even as the lengths change.

demo_steps.title: Recover the angle from a ratio
demo_steps.narration: Enter a ratio such as p/a = 0.7. The triangle snaps θ to arctan(0.7) ≈ 35° and names the relation, showing that two known side lengths are enough to recover the unknown acute angle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Side names are roles defined by theta, and any known pair of side lengths pins down theta through exactly one inverse trigonometric relation: arctan for p/a, arcsin for p/h, arccos for a/h.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Match the textbook figure: a plain black-outline right triangle with the right angle at the lower right (small open square), horizontal base labeled a centered below it, vertical right side labeled p outside it, hypotenuse labeled h above its midpoint, and an arc with the Greek letter θ at the left vertex. No axes, grid, numbers, or shading in the default state. Highlight the clicked side in a strong accent color (e.g. blue) with the θ arc echoing the same color, and fade in the role word (adjacent/opposite/hypotenuse) beside the side. When the slider or ratio drives theta, redraw the triangle continuously, keeping the base anchored at the left vertex and the right-angle marker square; show the current θ value in degrees near the arc and the active relation (e.g. θ = arctan(p/a)) as an annotation when a ratio is entered.

authoredContext:
Given two sides of a right triangle like the one shown in the figure, find an angle.

An illustration of a right triangle with an angle theta. Adjacent to theta is the side a, opposite theta is the side p, and the hypoteneuse is side h.
